description: Paintable, rapid, high modulus polyurethane sealant and adhesive
whereToUse: Mapeflex PU 45 FT has been specially developed for sealing expansion and distribution joints in horizontal and vertical surfaces, including those which are subject to occasional chemical attack by hydrocarbons.

It is also recommended for flexible bonds between similar and different materials most commonly used in the building industry for both internal and external applications and as a replacement or to compliment mechanical fasteners.
industrial floors subject to vehicular traffic, including heavy vehicles
concrete floors for internal and external car-parks, supermarkets, shopping centres and warehouses
concrete walls and general internal and external vertical structures where the use of a thixotropic product is required
Sealing pipe-work systems for air-conditioning and electric cables.
Sealing sheet-steel sections, such as flashing and guttering.
notFor: Do not use on dusty or flaky surfaces.
Do not use on damp surfaces.
Do not use to seal joints in stone and marble: use Mapesil LM or Mapesil Stone Matt.
Do not use on bituminous surfaces where the bleeding of oil may be present.
Do not apply Mapeflex PU 45 FT if the temperature is below +5°C.

notes: consumptionTable: the first row is the printed header (columns are 'Linear metres' per '300 ml kit' and per '600 ml kit'); the six rows after it are data, values in that column order. The first joint size is printed '5x5' without spaces. The same 12 figures are repeated one per entry in consumption. The 300 ml column is not exactly half the 600 ml column in the two largest sizes (25 x 12.5: 0.9 vs 1.9; 30 x 15: 0.6 vs 1.3), so the printed figures look rounded/truncated; a calculator should use the table values as printed rather than derive one column from the other. No formula is printed. The table calls the packs '300 ml kit' / '600 ml kit' while PACKAGING and the application text call them '300 ml cartridges' / '600 ml cartridges'; the body text also says 'metal cartridges and soft cartridges'. The word 'sausage' is not used. consumption also carries three joint-depth rule rows (from the WIDTH OF JOINT / DEPTH OF SEALANT table) and the 15 cm adhesive bead spacing; these are sizing figures, not rates, and are labelled as such in basis. For adhesive use the sheet gives no consumption figure: 'According to the bonding method used (formation of a bead or spot-application).' Classification wording differs inside the sheet: the body text gives the EN 15651-1 rating as 'F-EXT-INT CC' and the EN 15651-4 rating hyphenated across a line break ('PW-EXT-INT-' / 'CC'), while the technical data table prints 'F-EXT-INT-CC, class 20 HM' and 'PW-EXT-INT-CC, class 20 HM' (table form used in standards). ISO 11600 is given in the body as 'class F20 HM'. Movement capacity is printed two ways that agree: 'Elongation in service continuous use: 20%' and 'withstands movements when in service up to 20% of the average width of the sealed joint' (for more, the sheet says to use Mapeflex PU40). The sheet states more limits than the 5 kept in notFor, including: not on surfaces dirty with oil, grease or mould-stripping compounds; do not contaminate the wet surface with alcohol; 'Do not bond with layers of product more than 3 mm thick'; primer must be overcoated no later than 6 hours after application. whereToUse is a selection (8 of the sheet's items); the three unpunctuated items are sub-bullets of 'Sealing expansion and distribution joints subject to movements up to 20% of the average width of the joint in:'. Tensile strength and elongation at break rows are printed with the sub-label 'after 28 days at 23°C and 50% R.H.', dropped from the labels here. 'Dust dry: 35 mins.' is the nearest thing to a skin time; no separate skin-formation row is printed.
